scores.name: judge_quality
scores.detail: The output provides a specific, data-driven analysis identifying energy as the main driver of the CPI increase, with supporting detail on shelter, food, and core components. It includes historical context (2019 and 2022-23 cycles) and percentile positioning, stays well under 120 words (78), makes no forecasts or speculations about Fed motives, and remains neutral. All numbers are consistent with the input facts (0.4% MoM, 3.4% YoY, up from 3.3% prior) and the tool calls align with the reference requirements.

scores.name: judge_quality
scores.detail: The output accurately describes the FOMC decision (25bp cut to 4.00-4.25% with 1 dissent) and provides relevant context on inflation and unemployment that would drive such a decision. It cites specific data points (core PCE at 3.3% YoY in July, unemployment at 4.1% in August) that explain the rationale without speculating about Fed motives. The analysis is neutral, factual, and stays within the 120-word limit at 84 words. It appropriately compares current conditions to recent history (inflation above 2025 ranges, unemployment modestly higher than January low) to contextualize the cut.
